entries.title: keyring-rs — cross-platform credential storage library
entries.note: Maintained by open-source-cooperative (originally hwchen); now factored into keyring-core (API) and per-store crates. Supported platforms: macOS, iOS, Linux/BSD via Secret Service, Windows.

entries.title: keyring — Rust API docs
entries.note: Entry::new(service, user) is the canonical constructor; set_password/get_password/delete_credential are the core operations. apple-native and linux-native-sync-persistent features select platform backends.

entries.title: keyring-core — Cross-platform library for managing secrets
entries.note: Pure trait/error definitions split out from the keyring sample crate. Lets downstream callers depend on the abstraction without pulling all credential-store implementations.

entries.title: keychain-services.rs — Rust binding for macOS Keychain Services (experimental)
entries.note: Lower-level than keyring; exposes Secure Enclave / TouchID-gated keys. Warns that the macOS Keychain API requires signed code for many entitlements — apps without code-signing get MissingEntitlement errors.

entries.title: SecItemAdd(_:_:) — Apple Developer Documentation
entries.note: Primitive used by every macOS keychain wrapper; takes a CFDictionary of attributes (kSecClass, kSecAttrService, kSecAttrAccount, kSecValueData, kSecAttrAccessible).

entries.title: kSecAttrAccessible — Apple Developer Documentation
entries.note: Accessibility policy attribute on a keychain item. kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked is the default; AfterFirstUnlock and similar variants gate access on device state.

entries.title: Secret Service API Draft (org.freedesktop.Secret.*)
entries.note: Cross-desktop D-Bus protocol for password storage. Defines Service / Collection / Item / Session interfaces, OpenSession, default collection, lookup-attribute model.

entries.title: libsecret — GNOME secret storage client library
entries.note: Reference C client for the Secret Service D-Bus API; gnome-keyring and KWallet both implement the server side. Used (via FFI) by Rust's keyring crate on Linux/BSD.

entries.title: Use secret references with 1Password CLI
entries.note: Secret references take the form op://<vault>/<item>/[section/]<field>. op read, op inject, and op run all resolve them; op run injects into env vars for a subprocess.

entries.title: 1Password CLI (op) — overview
entries.note: op CLI commands: read, inject, run, item get. Reads gated by the desktop-app session (biometric unlock) or service account token.

entries.title: Securing MCP servers with 1Password: stop credential exposure
entries.note: Argues for runtime injection of MCP server secrets via op run instead of inlining in agent config. Aligned with our v1.1 OnePasswordStore design.

entries.title: Bitwarden CLI (bw) — Password Manager CLI documentation
entries.note: bw login + bw unlock yield a BW_SESSION env var; bw get password <name> and bw get item <id> return values/JSON. Session is required for every subsequent read.

entries.title: vault kv get — HashiCorp Vault CLI
entries.note: vault kv get -mount=secret -field=password <path> is the script-friendly form. KV v2 adds -version and metadata.

entries.title: Key/Value v2 — HashiCorp Vault secrets engine
entries.note: Versioned KV engine: versioning, soft delete, metadata, check-and-set. Critical prior art for any leased/TTL backend in v1.1+.

entries.title: doppler run — inject secrets as env vars
entries.note: doppler run -- <command> fetches the latest secrets for the configured project/environment and execs the command with them in env. Works across shells; multi-line supported.

entries.title: MCP security best practices for credentials, tokens, and secrets — Doppler
entries.note: Recommends runtime injection over .env, environment isolation per MCP server, and centralized rotation. Aligns with our daemon-injected env-var model.

entries.title: Infisical CLI run — inject secrets into subprocess
entries.note: infisical run --env=<env> --path=<path> -- <command> fetches and injects. Adds --prefix and multi --path flags for namespacing.

entries.title: aws secretsmanager get-secret-value — AWS CLI Reference
entries.note: Canonical API: aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id <arn-or-name> --query SecretString --output text. Identity sourced from the AWS_PROFILE / IAM role of the caller.

entries.title: gcloud secrets versions access — Google Cloud Secret Manager
entries.note: gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=<name> prints the secret. Uses ADC for auth; regional secrets require --location.

entries.title: az keyvault secret show — Azure CLI Reference
entries.note: az keyvault secret show --vault-name <vault> --name <secret> --query value -o tsv. Backed by Azure AD identity of the signed-in user or managed identity.

entries.title: SecretSpec — declarative secrets manifest, multiple providers
entries.note: Separates declaration (secretspec.toml) from storage backend. Providers: OnePassword, .env, env, GCP Secret Manager, system keyring, LastPass, pass(1). Architecture mirrors what we want for the SecretStore trait.

entries.title: secrecy — wrapper types that prevent accidental secret exposure
entries.note: SecretBox/SecretString/SecretVec — implements Debug as [REDACTED], drops via zeroize. Use as the in-process carrier for all secret values.

entries.title: zeroize — secure memory wipe primitive
entries.note: core::ptr::write_volatile + atomic fences. Pure Rust, no FFI. Backbone of secrecy.

entries.title: rpassword — getpass()-style password prompt for Rust
entries.note: Cross-platform terminal input with echo disabled. Defaults to reading from /dev/tty, not stdin, so it works correctly when stdin is redirected.

entries.title: How to Handle Secrets on the Command Line — smallstep
entries.note: Survey of why argv is the wrong place for secrets (process list, shell history, CI logs), and the safe alternatives: stdin, file paths, env-by-reference.

entries.title: How to Handle Secrets at the Command Line — GitGuardian
entries.note: Cheat sheet of safe vs unsafe CLI patterns; identifies --password-stdin and credential files as canonical safe forms.

entries.title: VS Code SecretStorage API
entries.note: Per-extension secret storage. Backed by Keychain on macOS, libsecret on Linux, Credential Manager on Windows (via Electron safeStorage). Precedent for what an editor expects.

entries.title: SOPS — Secrets OPerationS
entries.note: File-based encrypted secrets — YAML/JSON/ENV/INI. Backends: AWS/GCP/Azure KMS, age, PGP. Not a runtime fetcher; an at-rest format.

entries.title: agenix — age-encrypted secrets for NixOS
entries.note: NixOS-native pattern: encrypt at rest with age, decrypt on activation, mount under /run/agenix with restrictive perms. Inspiration for the file-mount form a future store could adopt.

entries.title: MCP01:2025 — Token Mismanagement and Secret Exposure (OWASP)
entries.note: Top entry in the OWASP MCP Top 10 for 2025. Lists the failure modes our threat model must defend against: argv leakage, .env commits, oversharing tokens between servers.

entries.title: Goose — config and OS keyring integration
entries.note: Goose stores LLM provider keys in the OS keyring by default; GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING falls back to env vars. Closest prior art in the MCP-host space to our approach.

entries.title: MCP server security: secrets management and architecture — Doppler
entries.note: Argues for environment-variable isolation per MCP server and for fetching at server-spawn rather than agent-launch. Validates our daemon-injected model.
